title: Illustration / Characters / Eyes
slide_intent: Choose a clear geometric eye style that suits the character’s viewing scale so expression remains readable.
strategic_value: A small family of eye treatments can give Duolingo’s cast visual variety while maintaining a common illustration language.
demonstration: Five labeled heads show Round, Glasses, Almond, Linear and Dots eye styles, with an asterisk on Dots and guidance at right.
practical_value: Select an eye treatment by character and intended scale; reserve dot eyes for characters that always appear small.

content_islands.name: Eye-style family
content_islands.spec: Arrange three labeled heads in the top row and two below at left; retain the Dots asterisk.

content_islands.name: Style and scale conditions
content_islands.spec: Place the Eyes heading, geometric-style instruction and dot-eye footnote at right.

reference_purposes.Expression: Five distinct eye treatments show a consistent geometric family.
reference_purposes.Application: The labeled specimens provide a choice of treatments for character design.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source permits other geometric styles but excludes ovals; dot eyes are only recommended for a character that always appears at small scale.

ingredient.name: Geometric eye styles
ingredient.role: Keep facial expression recognizable at the intended scale.
ingredient.application: Choose among the displayed eye families or explore other geometric styles; avoid ovals and use dot eyes only when the character always appears small.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. The five styles are the main families, not an exhaustive permitted list. Dot eyes carry a recommendation tied to persistent small-scale use.
